subject: german
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'We have to wear a uniform'?
questions.explain: 'Tragen' here means 'to wear' and 'müssen' = 'to have to', so this is 'We have to wear a uniform'.
'Der Lebenslauf' means 'the CV/résumé' (literally 'course of life').
'Die Werbung' means 'advertising/adverts'.
False friend: 'das Gymnasium' is a 'grammar school'. A gym is 'die Turnhalle'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'Yesterday I worked a lot' (past)?
questions.explain: 'Habe... gearbeitet' is the perfect tense 'worked'; with 'gestern' (yesterday) the perfect is correct, and the past participle goes to the end.

questions.q: How do you say 'The work was very tiring'?
questions.explain: 'Anstrengend' = 'tiring/strenuous' and 'war' = 'was'.
'Ein Sänger' is a male singer (female: 'eine Sängerin'); 'a song' is 'ein Lied'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I find chemistry difficult'?
questions.explain: 'Schwierig' = 'difficult'; 'einfach' (easy) and 'langweilig' (boring) are distractors.
'Der Lehrer' is a male teacher (female: 'die Lehrerin'); 'leer' (empty) is the near-miss.

questions.q: How do you say 'I would like to become an engineer'?
questions.explain: 'Moechte ... werden' = 'would like to become'; 'der Ingenieur' = engineer.
'Das Zeugnis' means 'the (school) report/report card'.
False friend: 'die Note' is a school 'grade/mark' (e.g. 'eine gute Note'), not an English 'note'.

questions.q: What does 'streng' mean (e.g. of a teacher)?
questions.explain: 'Streng' means 'strict'; 'eine strenge Lehrerin' = 'a strict teacher'.
'Das Fach' means 'a (school) subject', e.g. 'mein Lieblingsfach' = 'my favourite subject'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'School starts at quarter past eight'?
options: Die Schule beginnt um Viertel vor acht
Die Schule beginnt um Viertel nach acht
Die Schule endet um Viertel nach acht
Die Schule beginnt um halb acht
questions.explain: 'Viertel nach acht' = 'quarter past eight'; 'vor' (to) is the distractor.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I dream of a well-paid job'?
options: Ich träume von einem gut bezahlten Job
Ich träume von einem langweiligen Job
Ich suche einen gut bezahlten Job
Ich habe einen gut bezahlten Job
questions.explain: 'Träumen von' = 'to dream of' and 'gut bezahlt' = 'well-paid'.
'Selbststaendig' means 'self-employed/independent'.
'Die Bewerbung' means 'the (job) application'; 'sich bewerben' = to apply.
'Die sozialen Medien' means 'social media' (also 'soziale Netzwerke' = social networks).

questions.q: Which sentence means 'Later I would like to work abroad'?
options: Später möchte ich im Ausland arbeiten
Früher wollte ich im Ausland arbeiten
Später möchte ich im Ausland wohnen
Später muss ich zu Hause arbeiten
questions.explain: 'Später' = 'later', 'möchte... arbeiten' = 'would like to work', 'im Ausland' = 'abroad'.
'Verdienen' usually means 'to earn' (money), e.g. 'Geld verdienen'.
'Der Beruf' means 'the profession/occupation', e.g. 'Was sind Sie von Beruf?' = 'What's your job?'.
